question: What challenges does the multi-messager astrophysics (MMA) approach currently meet for detecting astrophysical phenomena?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer must identify the enormous data volumes generated by MMA facilities as a central challenge, citing e.g. LSST's ~30 terabytes of pipeline-processed data per night or its trillion-line database on 20 billion objects over ten years.
examples: LSST will produce 30 terabytes of processed data each night, straining analysis pipelines
Ten years of LSST operations yield a trillion-row database on 20 billion objects

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer must note that expanding detector networks probe larger volumes of space and increase detection rates, citing GWTC-1 merger rates (BNS 110–3840 Gpc^-3 yr^-1, BBH 9.7–101 Gpc^-3 yr^-1, NSBH upper bound ~610 Gpc^-3 yr^-1) or the ~one GW detection per 15 days of searched data in O1–O2.
examples: BNS rates up to 3840 Gpc^-3 yr^-1 imply frequent triggers for follow-up
O1 and O2 averaged one GW detection per 15 days of searched data

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer must state that despite expectations, only one joint GW+EM detection (GW170817) has occurred, with no associated neutrino detection—plausibly due to an off-axis or low-luminosity GRB—showing how rarely all messengers are captured together.
examples: GW170817 remains the only confirmed joint GW–EM counterpart
No high-energy neutrinos were detected by ANTARES, IceCube, or Auger; the non-detection is consistent with an off-axis GRB

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer must explain that detector geometry and a source's sky position constrain sensitivity, e.g., GW170817 was well above the horizon for IceCube and ANTARES (limiting sensitivity below ~100 TeV) while nearly ideal for Auger, with roughly a factor of 10 fluence-sensitivity gain expected for favorable near-horizon locations.
examples: IceCube and ANTARES had reduced sensitivity to GW170817 because it was above their horizon
A factor of ~10 neutrino fluence-sensitivity improvement is expected for near-horizon source locations

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer must indicate that existing computational resources and data-analysis tools are already stretched to handle current MMA data volumes, requiring faster, more efficient algorithms and low-latency automated alert pipelines.
examples: Current computing resources and cyber-infrastructure cannot keep pace with MMA data streams and speed requirements
Automated, low-latency alert pipelines are needed instead of manual follow-up

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: The answer must highlight delays in the response chain, citing that manual EM follow-up of GW170817 began ~8 hours after the GW signal, when some early EM emission was no longer observable, and the need for rapid GW alerts to enable timely multi-messenger searches.
examples: Eight hours elapsed before GW170817 received EM follow-up; key early emission had faded
Issuing GW alerts as early as possible is essential for coordinated follow-up

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer should mention that GWs from BNS/NSBH mergers can be detected up to ~15 minutes before coalescence in advanced LIGO/Virgo, offering an early-warning window that could substantially improve follow-up coordination and is currently underexploited.
examples: Advanced detectors can register BNS inspiral signals up to 15 minutes before merger
Early GW alerts would let telescopes prepare for pre-merger pointings

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer should explain why joint detections matter scientifically, e.g., that early EM observations of BNS/NSBH mergers probe ejected material and r-process nucleosynthesis, and that compact mergers are expected triple-messenger (GW, photon, neutrino) sources.
examples: Early EM counterparts constrain ejecta properties and r-process nucleosynthesis
BNS mergers are expected to emit gravitational waves, light, and neutrinos

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer should frame the overall challenge as fully exploiting the enormous physical and financial investment in MMA facilities through comprehensive data analysis, whose potential may be underutilized without adequate tools.
examples: The full potential of the enormous facility investment risks being lost to data-analysis bottlenecks
Realizing MMA's promise requires worldwide participation in and utilization of all data products
